facts.value: no later than the employer's usual regularly scheduled payroll date
facts.summary: Wyoming: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due no later than the employer's usual regularly scheduled payroll date.
facts.evidence_quote: (a) Whenever an employee quits service or is discharged, the employee shall be paid whatever wages are due him ... no later than the employer's usual practice on regularly scheduled payroll dates or at a time specified under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement

facts.summary: Wyoming: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due no later than the employer's usual regularly scheduled payroll date.
facts.evidence_quote: (a) Whenever an employee quits service or is discharged, the employee shall be paid whatever wages are due him ... no later than the employer's usual practice on regularly scheduled payroll dates or at a time specified under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Wyoming state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $5.15. Employers covered by the federal FLSA must pay at least $7.25.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $5.15 Employers subject to the Fair Labor Standards Act must pay the current Federal minimum wage of $7.25 per hour.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page. The FLSA federal minimum of $7.25 per hour applies to covered employers, so $5.15 applies only to the few employers not covered by the FLSA.

facts.summary: Wyoming base new employer UI rate: Industry average (IndAvg).
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance
facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. Footnote 4: new employer rate shown is the base rate; higher rates may apply by industry or other factors. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law. IndAvg means the new employer rate is the industry average rate; get the exact rate from the state agency. Rate basis: DOL base rate. It may exclude mandatory surcharges, fund-building rates and assessments; check the state agency or total_new_employer_rate where available.

facts.value: Yes: most employers must obtain coverage from the WY DWS Workers' Compensation Division; certain employers and employee groups are exempt and may buy private coverage.
facts.summary: Wyoming is a monopolistic state: most employers must get workers' comp from the state fund (DWS Workers' Compensation Division); exempt employers and groups may buy private coverage.
facts.evidence_quote: In Wyoming, most employers must obtain workers' compensation coverage through the Department of Workforce Service Workers' Compensation Division. This is because Wyoming is a monopolistic state, where the state fund is the primary provider of this insurance. However, certain employers and employee groups are exempt from this requirement. These exempt employers may purchase workers' compensation insurance from private insurers on the open market
